text:
Brayden Schenn is 35, has a Stanley Cup ring from St. Louis and more than 1,100 games behind him, and he is still doing the thing he has always done: going to the hard areas. His 5.22 individual expected goals rank as real chance creation, and his five goals sit almost exactly on that number. Nothing about his scoring looks borrowed.

Twelve points in 17 games is a solid second-season line for an Islander playing about 17 minutes a night. The 5v5 shot share is under water (47% of attempts) but the chance quality is even, which fits a forward who shoots from close.

The New York Post wrote this month that he has fulfilled a leadership role for the Islanders, and Schenn himself was quoted by NHL.com's Stefen Rosner praising a young linemate as someone who "goes to hard areas, wins battles." That is a fair description of Schenn, too.

The caution: Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. What he gives is honest; the ceiling at this age is the open question.
headline: Schenn, at 35, still finds the net front
